newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen mostly dry through weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen mostly dry through weekend.

text.p: The U.S. Midwest should be mostly rain-free through the weekend after a storm system now over Minnsota, Wisconsin and northern Indiana moves east, meteorologists said.

The storm system dumped up to three inches of rain late Tuesday and early Wednesday across southern Minnesota and should bring rain to Wisconsin, Michigan, northern Indiana and Ohio Wednesday before exiting the area.
"Between now and Monday there is not much shower activity in the forecast for the Midwest," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
A cool front entering the Midwest may keep high temperatures in the upper 70s to low 80s degrees Fahrenheit through the weekend, meteorologists said.
More showers were likely next week in the Midwest, but amounts and coverage were not available.
"About six days from now it looks like a much wetter time for the Midwest," said Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis Inc meteorologist.
